Fix module resolution for transitive dependencies in SemanticAnalyzer

## Problem
When importing modules like `std::mem` that have their own imports,
the compiler failed with "unknown type" errors for types from
transitive dependencies:

```
error[E0020]: unknown type ''ExecError''
```

Even though ExecError was defined in std::error (which std::mem imports),
it wasn''t available during semantic analysis of std::mem''s function
signatures.

## Root Cause
Two issues in SemanticAnalyzer:

1. **Missing transitive imports**: When processing `from std::mem import X`,
   the analyzer didn''t load std::mem''s own imports first, so types like
   ExecError (from std::error) were unavailable.

2. **Incomplete struct registration**: Only explicitly imported structs
   were registered, but other public structs referenced in method
   signatures weren''t available, causing "unknown type" errors.

## Solution
Modified SemanticAnalyzer.cs:

1. **Process transitive imports** (lines 250-257):
   - Before analyzing an imported module, first process its imports
   - Matches ImportResolver behavior that IrBuilder uses successfully
   - Ensures all dependency types are available

2. **Register all public structs** (lines 348-377):
   - Changed to register ALL pub structs from imported modules
   - Not just explicitly imported ones
   - Ensures types referenced in signatures are available

## Verification
- ✅ Test case `from std::mem import MemoryBlock` now compiles
- ✅ Shows "✓ Compiled 4 modules" (std::core, std::mem, std::error loaded)
- ✅ Test suite: 962/964 tests pass (99.8% pass rate)
- ✅ No new regressions introduced

The 2 failing tests have pre-existing linking issues unrelated to this fix.
